newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan textile group concerned about EU probe.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan textile group concerned about EU probe.

text.p: The national organisation of Pakistan's textile mills voiced concern on Monday over an anti-dumping investigation ordered by the European Union into exports of Pakistani fabrics, calling the move a harassment.

An official of All Pakistan Textile Mills Association asked the Pakistani government at a news conference to approach the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to seek a remedy for what he called misuse of WTO laws for "harassment and industrial arm-twisting".

"The ongoing anti-dumping investigation by the European Union against the export of cotton fabrics from Pakistan is a matter of grave concern for our textile industry in particular and the country in general," said Akber Sheikh, convenor of APTMA's committee on WTO.

He said many discrepancies in the WTO laws had led to the imposition of anti-dumping duties of 30 percent on Pakistani products while duties of around 15 percent had been imposed on other countries, including India, Egypt, Indonesia and Turkey.

"The WTO laws have become a tool of harassment and industrial arm twisting," he said, referring to the EU investigation ordered last month on suspicion that Pakistani cotton fabrics were being sold at prices below cost.
